title: Nine slow nights from Samsing to Jayanti
start: NJP railway station or Bagdogra airport
end: NJP railway station or Bagdogra airport

cost_split.item: Reserved car with driver, 10 days, half share
Forest lodges, good hotels and riverside rooms, 9 nights with meals
Private safari jeeps in five parks and elephant safari if running, half share
Local guides for Samsing and the Mahakal cave walk

meta_description: 9 nights across the Dooars by private car: Samsing's tea hills, Murti for Gorumara, Jaldapara, Chilapata and Jayanti in Buxa, from ₹51,000 per person.
summary: The Dooars at walking pace, for people with time: two nights in Samsing's tea hills, two on the Murti for Gorumara and Chapramari, two at Madarihat for Jaldapara, one in Chilapata forest and two on the Jayanti riverbed inside Buxa Tiger Reserve. Your own car, private jeeps and the best rooms available. About ₹51,000 per person for two.
intro: Nine nights is long enough that the Dooars stop being a checklist. You can spend a whole morning in a tea garden at Samsing, skip a safari when you are tired, and sit on the Jayanti riverbed until the hills across in Bhutan turn dark. Each base has two nights except Chilapata, so you unpack only five times.

The route runs west to east, from the hills above Chalsa down to the parks and on to Buxa, then back to NJP in one long drive of about five hours. The car and private jeeps are the main costs. Floods in October 2025 hit Gorumara and shut Jaldapara for a time, and all the parks close from mid-June to mid-September. Check current status before you travel.
highlights: Two cool nights among Samsing's tea
Gorumara and Chapramari from the Murti riverbank
Jaldapara's rhinos from a private jeep
The Jayanti riverbed and the walk to the Mahakal cave

days.title: NJP to Samsing
days.text: Your driver meets you at NJP or Bagdogra. Cross the Teesta at Sevoke, drive through Malbazar and Chalsa and climb through tea gardens to Samsing, at about 900 m, on the southern edge of Neora Valley National Park. Check in at the forest corporation's Samsing centre or a good resort on the Rocky Island road. Late afternoon walk on the garden roads, looking down over the plain.

days.title: Rocky Island and Suntalekhola
days.text: A morning walk with a local guide on the forest edge above the village, for birds and views. After lunch, drive down to Rocky Island, where the Murti runs between huge boulders, then 5 km on to Suntalekhola to cross the hanging footbridge over the stream from Neora Valley. Back to Samsing for tea as the sun drops behind the hills.

days.title: Down to Murti, Chapramari at dusk
days.text: Drive down out of the hills to Murti and check into the best grade at the forest corporation's Murti Banani centre on the river. Rest through the middle of the day. In the late afternoon, take a private jeep to the Chapramari watchtower over the forest waterhole, known for the largest gaur herds in West Bengal and often visited by elephants.

days.title: Gorumara at dawn and Dhupjhora
days.text: The driver takes you to the Lataguri counter for a private dawn jeep to a Gorumara watchtower, Jatraprasad, the Rhino Observation Point or Medla by bullock cart, over grassland and salt licks. Back for breakfast. Late morning, visit the forest department's elephants at Dhupjhora. Afternoon on the Murti riverbed with binoculars, or a nap.

days.title: Through the tea gardens to Madarihat
days.text: Drive east through Chalsa, Nagrakata and Birpara among the big Dooars tea gardens, stopping to watch plucking in season. Check into the WBTDC Jaldapara Tourist Lodge or a good hotel in Madarihat. Confirm the morning safari and ask whether elephant safaris are running. A quiet evening.

days.title: Jaldapara and Totopara
days.text: A private jeep at first light into the Torsa grassland, where Jaldapara's roughly 330 rhinos graze in the open; take the elephant safari instead if it is running. Back for breakfast and a rest. In the afternoon, drive about 22 km to Totopara, home of the Toto community, and visit quietly, asking before photographs.

days.title: Chilapata forest
days.text: A short drive to the forest corporation's Mendabari Jungle Lodge. In the afternoon, a private jeep through dense forest to Nalraja Garh, the brick ruins of an early frontier fort, and along the elephant corridor between Jaldapara and Buxa. Elephants are often near the track at dusk. Dinner at the lodge and an early night.

days.title: To Jayanti on its river
days.text: Drive east via Hasimara and Rajabhatkhawa into Buxa Tiger Reserve to Jayanti. Check into the best riverside room or cottage you can find; ask for a view of the river, which spreads into a pale bed of stones below the Bhutan hills. In the afternoon, take a private jeep safari in Buxa from Jayanti, or simply sit on the riverbed until dark.

days.title: Mahakal cave walk
days.text: Walk with a local guide up the riverbed and through forest towards the Mahakal cave, a limestone cave revered as a Shiva shrine; local accounts put it at about 5–6 km each way, with some scrambling. If that is too much, take the shorter walk along the river with the guide and turn back when you like. Afternoon rest and a last evening on the river.

days.title: Jayanti to NJP
days.text: An early breakfast and the long drive west along the highway through Hasimara, Birpara and Malbazar to Siliguri. Stop for lunch on the way. Reach NJP or Bagdogra by mid-afternoon. This is the longest drive of the trip, so do not book anything before evening, and keep a buffer for highway traffic.

includes: Reserved car with driver for 10 days from NJP or Bagdogra and back
Nine nights in forest corporation lodges, the WBTDC lodge, good hotels and riverside rooms, with meals
Private jeep safaris in Chapramari, Gorumara, Jaldapara, Chilapata and Buxa, with fees
Local guides at Samsing and Jayanti
excludes: Buxa Fort walk (can be added from Santalabari)
save_money: Travel as four in one car; the car is the largest cost and is the same for two or four.
Choose family homestays at Samsing and Jayanti, which cost about half the best rooms there.
Drop one of the five safaris; most people see plenty in three or four.
good_to_know: Parks close from about 16 June to 15 September; check current status before you travel.
Floods in October 2025 damaged parts of Gorumara and shut Jaldapara for a time; check current status before you travel.
Hollong lodge inside Jaldapara burned in June 2024; do not book it unless reopening is confirmed.
Jayanti gets busy around Shivaratri; book rooms early for those dates.

faqs.q: Is nine nights in the Dooars too much?
faqs.a: For most people a week is plenty, but nine nights suits those who want to slow down, travel with older parents or photograph wildlife properly. Two nights at most stops means less packing and more time on riverbeds and in tea gardens.

faqs.q: How much does a 10-day car cost?
faqs.a: Roughly ₹28,000–32,000 for a car with driver from NJP and back in 2025–26, depending on the vehicle and season. Split between two, about ₹15,000 each; between four, half that. Drivers' stays and meals are usually included in the rate; confirm when you book.

Yes. From Jayanti, drive about 30 km to Santalabari and walk the 5 km stone path up to the fort, about two hours each way. It makes a full day. Swap it for the Mahakal walk, or add a night in a Buxa homestay.

Jayanti is a forest village inside Buxa Tiger Reserve on a river that spreads into a wide bed of pale stones below the Bhutan hills. There are homestays, small lodges and some private cottages. Evenings on the riverbed are the main attraction.

faqs.q: Is this trip good for photographers?
faqs.a: Very. You get grassland rhinos at Jaldapara, watchtower views at Gorumara, gaur at Chapramari, dense forest at Chilapata, tea gardens at Samsing and river landscapes at Jayanti. Dawn and dusk light in winter is soft and misty. Camera fees apply in parks.

Yes. The drives are short except the first and last days, rooms are on flat ground, and safaris are in jeeps. The Mahakal walk is optional and can be shortened. Plan midday rests and carry any medicines, as pharmacies are only in the bigger towns.

faqs.q: Will we see tigers in Buxa?
faqs.a: Almost certainly not. Buxa is a tiger reserve, but tigers there are extremely rare. Expect elephants, gaur, deer, many birds and beautiful forest. Rhinos are best seen at Jaldapara and Gorumara.

faqs.q: What if a park is closed?
faqs.a: Parks close for the monsoon from about mid-June to mid-September and may close briefly after floods or for census work. If one is closed, swap its safari for another park or a river walk. Check current status before you travel.

Yes. ATMs are available in Malbazar, Madarihat, Hasimara and Alipurduar, but not in Samsing, Murti, Chilapata or Jayanti, and card machines are unreliable. UPI works where network does. Carry enough for tips, guides and snacks.
